note: Women working the Eighth Ave strip and hotel bars. Content rule: barks are about weather, cops, money, feet, friends. Nothing sexual.

lines.text: Evening, sugar. You lost or just walking slow?
Hey, Del's friend. You look tired. Everybody looks tired.
You a cop? You walk like a cop. Relax your shoulders.
My feet hurt in two languages.
Rent's due. Tax is due. Everything's due but me.
Brannock's car went by twice. Twice means he's hungry.
Tina says she's doing hair by Christmas. I'd let her do mine.
Saving up for a sofa. A real one. With legs.
Fifty a week to stand on a sidewalk the city owns.
Cops on Monday, Lonnie on Tuesday. Who's Wednesday?
Somebody stole my good umbrella. In July. Who does that?
Rain. There goes the hair. There goes the night.
Wet night, slow night. Coffee at the Royal, anybody?
Rain's good for one thing. Cops stay in the car.
Hot enough to fry an egg on the hood of a squad car.
Hundred degrees and they want us in nylons.
Keep honking, mister. I'm deaf in that ear anyway.
Horn don't make you handsome.
Watch the shoes! These cost more than your car.
Excuse you.
Who's chasing you? Should I be running too?
Run, baby, run. Nobody runs on Eighth for good news.
Get off the curb, you maniac!
Lights out. Everybody stay where Marcus can see you.
Dark street, dark business. Go home, girls.
Four a.m. Pie at the Royal. Best part of the night.
Walk me to the bus? No? Okay. Next time.
I got a kid in Catholic school. Every dollar, Catholic school.
Club meets Sunday. Bring your five. Bring your sister.
Rule number one, says Del: count everything. Rule two: count it again.
Lonnie says he's protection. From what? From Lonnie?
Morning, Marcus! Yes, I know it's morning. Barely.
